A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLB-OMD research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison. Relocated material was matched, including v1 Appendix D with v2 Appendix A.3.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix F report original logistic-bandit and Poisson-bandit simulations and Covertype experiments, including regret and runtime results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original simulations and Covertype results, together with an added comparison of parameter-estimation confidence regions.

M1.justification: The OMD update, Hessian accumulation, and UCB action rule remain. However, v2 revises the regularization and confidence-radius prescriptions used by Algorithm 1, including removing the requirement λ ≥ 2Cμ/g(τ). This changes the method's confidence-set calibration without introducing a new estimator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate logistic bandits, Poisson bandits, and the same Covertype-derived task. The new confidence-region diagnostic changes dimensionality and horizon within existing coverage; it does not introduce a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain GLM-UCB, GLOC, RS-GLinCB, and OFUGLB, with ECOLog and OFULog-r additionally used for logistic bandits and Covertype. The new diagnostic uses existing comparators. v2 explains the exclusion of OFUL-MLogB, which was already absent from v1's empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: The added confidence-region experiment in v2 Figure 3 specifies d = 2, T = 300, and S = 3, 5, 7. Retained experiments preserve their documented horizons, Covertype preprocessing and clustering, and practical regularization conventions. Changed curves alone do not establish further protocol changes.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a diagnostic comparing the confidence-region sizes of GLB-OMD, OFUGLB, and GLM-UCB across three parameter norms. The larger-S regret and runtime sensitivity analyses were already present in v1 Appendix F.2.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages over 10 independent trials but does not define the displayed uncertainty. v2 Appendices E.1 and E.3 identify shaded regions and error bars as 99% confidence intervals and specify different random seeds. This is additional reporting, not evidence of an increased run count.

E6.justification: Reported synthetic-regret curves change substantially in Figures 1–2 and the larger-S appendix plots. For example, Figure 2a changes from GLB-OMD having higher regret than OFUGLB to lower regret. v2 also adds confidence-region results. Covertype results, including numerical runtime labels, are retained. The PDFs do not explain the curve revisions sufficiently to establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the auxiliary Gaussian covariance from αHs^-1 to αHs+1^-1 and changes the KL and log-determinant argument in Lemmas 6–7, propagating revised constants into the confidence bound. The assumptions and asymptotic regret rate remain. v2 also introduces a discrepancy: Theorem 1 omits the factor t from its logarithmic radius term, while Appendix A.1 retains it.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: a one-pass OMD estimator with a mix-loss-based confidence analysis, nearly optimal GLB regret, and time-independent per-round update costs. The additional evidence and comparisons do not replace these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses infinite-arm UCB optimization as a remaining computational bottleneck and Thompson sampling for convex arm sets. Appendix E.2 changes the explanation of OFUGLB's S-dependent runtime from maximum-likelihood optimization to arm-selection optimization. It also interprets the newly added confidence-region comparison.

D1.justification: Appendix E.1 newly identifies Python's time library as the runtime measurement tool. Hardware, SciPy and pseudoinverse implementation details, practical regularization conventions, and Covertype processing are retained. The computational-cost derivation moves from Appendix D to Appendix A.3 rather than being newly supplied.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 4.2 substantially expand positioning of the central analysis against concurrent work by Kirschner et al. and Clerico et al. They acknowledge related mix-loss confidence constructions and distinguish the evolving OMD estimator from MLE-based approaches. Additional foundational attribution includes Ville, Grünwald, and Faury et al. (2020).

P1.justification: v2 rewrites portions of the introduction, expands explanatory discussion, adds acknowledgments, and changes Cμ notation to Lμ. It relocates computational-cost material into Appendix A.3 and renumbers subsequent appendices. The six-section main narrative and most exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout throughout, changing typography, text width, spacing, title formatting, theorem boxes, and display placement. Synthetic plots are redrawn with revised ticks and styling, including a new inset in Figure 2a. A new three-panel confidence-region figure is added; v1 Figures 3–4 become v2 Figures 4–5.

improvement.justification: v2 improves uncertainty documentation, explains computational limitations more clearly, adds an informative diagnostic, and better situates its central technique. However, its revised Theorem 1 prints log(1 + Lμ/(λg(τ))) where Appendix A.1 derives log(1 + Lμt/(λg(τ))), creating a new inconsistency in the confidence-set prescription. Together with unexplained revisions to central regret curves, this prevents a reliable net-quality judgment despite the reporting gains.
